review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Everyday monetary amounts, income, spending, budgets and savings; repair payment terminology and duplicate price evaluations.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet. Retain CC BY 4.0 and underlying Princeton notices in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. CFPB financial-education material, Bank of England explanations and Gramota spelling evidence support selected terms. Labels and graph classifications are reviewed adaptations.
review.context_policy: All additions use U1 and unspecified strength. Existing home contexts and grammar remain unchanged. U4 loan, property and money records are not merged into physical cash or payment quantities.

sense_decisions.scope: Costly in the high-price sense duplicates the existing expensive evaluation, not a separate price quantity.
Inexpensive duplicates the existing cheap price evaluation; its parent expensive is wrong.
The neuter adjective duplicate becomes a leaf after its two reviewed children are consolidated; reuse the existing expensive evaluation.
A quantity expressed in monetary units, distinct from the money resource, cash objects and monetary funds. Do not copy the dictionary asset genus for a numerical amount.
A monetary amount accruing or received as income over a period. Separate this from arrival, gross receipts that merely exchange assets, and any jurisdiction-specific taxable-income rule.
Income accruing to an individual, with no tax-law threshold or filing rule inferred.
Income arising from paid work, including employment and self-employment in the selected everyday sense. Tax definitions and eligibility categories are not imported.
Personal income from sources other than current paid work. The accounting deferred-revenue meaning of unearned income/revenue is excluded.
Monetary remuneration for employment. Restrict the dictionary remuneration cluster to employee pay; exclude compensation for damages and business net profit.

sense_decisions.alignment: split from broad dictionary remuneration cluster
sense_decisions.scope: Employee pay specified as a fixed amount for a work period. Overtime, bonuses and deduction rules are not inferred for all employment.
Employee remuneration calculated from a rate per hour and the paid working time; no statutory minimum rate is asserted.
Employee pay before applicable deductions. Do not treat this restricted payroll quantity as every possible gross-income sense.
Employee pay remaining after applicable deductions. It is not the business-profit meaning of net income.
An amount of money spent, distinct from the spending action and from a general consumption of time or material. Do not import the tax-deductible-only expense sense.
A recurring budget expense expected to stay at a similar amount during the relevant periods. This is not a universal monthly schedule or an accounting fixed-cost definition.
A budget expense whose amount varies across the selected periods. Do not confuse this with a business cost varying with production volume.
Cost expressed as a monetary amount. This is narrower than the dictionary cost that also includes time or effort; it is not identical to selling price or to the verb cost.
The monetary charge or return for use of money, including borrowing and deposit contexts. It is not curiosity, a percentage ratio, or necessarily a fixed charge.
A rate specifying interest relative to a monetary base for a stated period and convention. Do not equate the rate with the charged amount, the abstract numerical percentage, APR or APY.
A plan allocating expected monetary resources among spending and saving over a period. Distinct from an allocated fund; forecasts are not assertions that transactions have happened.
A budget plan for one person.
A budget plan for a household, which need not coincide with an individual or legally defined family.
Money set aside for a purpose, narrower than the existing general fund/reserve. The fund has an amount; it is not the amount quantity itself.
Money retained for later use. Separate the accumulated resource from the act of saving and from a bank-account product.
A reserve for unexpected necessary expenses. No recommended reserve size, investment, or guaranteed protection is asserted.
Money allocated to a purpose, distinct from the budget plan and from a numerical monetary amount.
Organizing the use of monetary resources, including planning spending and saving. This is an everyday activity, not an investment service or IT memory management.
Planning the allocation of monetary resources. The selected process uses planning rather than the dictionary calculation-only parent.
Setting money aside for later use. Distinct from rescue, general preservation, cost cutting and the accumulated savings resource.
The monetary spending process, narrower than the existing general spending action. The monetary amount spent is a separate quantity.
Reuse high-price evaluation and consolidate duplicate adjective records.
Reuse low-price evaluation; preserve its existing opposition to expensive.
Reuse payment amount with a quantity genus and move verbs to action 7752.
Repair the malformed payment action and its physical-motion genus.
Reuse monetary price; do not import cost/sacrifice/value synonyms.
Broaden the medium-specific text genus to information object, retaining the existing plan ID.
Reuse planning as the genus for budgeting.
Reuse general fund/reserve; specialize only the new monetary fund.
Money in the legal-property universe remains the resource anchor; do not equate it with an amount or physical cash.
The artifact/wallet money record suggests cash, but its sense distinction from 1957 requires a separate reviewed cohort.
Loan as a legal contract is not automatically the loan amount, borrowing action or financial debt.
Duty remains distinct from financial debt.
Mental interest remains distinct from a monetary interest charge.
To interest remains a separate action.
The verb cost remains distinct from the monetary cost quantity.
The wealth-state record is not a monetary fund or income amount.
Keep general spending broader than the new monetary spending process.
General preservation and its malformed terms require a wider review.
General saving/preserving is not automatically saving money.
The numerical percentage ratio is distinct from a financial interest-rate quantity.
Deferred/unearned revenue is not the selected personal-income meaning.
Business profit/net income is distinct from employee net pay; accounting recognition needs separate review.
Tax deductibility is not a defining property of every household monetary expenditure.

review.limits: This is everyday financial vocabulary, not tax/accounting rules or financial advice. Jurisdictional deductions, interest formulas, legal tender requirements, debt contracts, currency systems, bank accounts, and investment recommendations are not encoded. Money records 1957/2413, wider wealth/economic-good hierarchies, general saving and expenditure processes, and loan/debt distinctions remain pending. Budget entries are plans, not factual future transactions. No application test suites.
review.staged_leaf_merges: 8285 and 9911 are independent leaves. Their archived genus edges are removed first; 5671 then has only its own archived genus. No facts or negations are discarded. All source concept/term rows and the union of all three original edges are preserved in this manifest.

collision_decisions.income_amount: Remove the erroneous income term from arrival 3365; retain that arrival concept and all its other terms and relations.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Exact normalized English spellings are candidates, not semantic identities or a missing-concept count.
